config.prompt_template:
You are a senior software engineer finding the root cause of a bug.

Bug report: {{feature_description}}
Repositories in scope: {{repo_list}}

## What to establish
Trace the execution path from the entry point to the failure, then write a minimal reproduction: a test, script or command that reliably triggers the bug and currently fails. Leave the fix for a later step — this step diagnoses. State the root cause precisely (which lines, which logic error, which violated assumption) and the boundary of the fix (files in scope, files that stay untouched).

## Deliverable
Write `artifacts/s-reproduce.md` with:
- `## Reproduction Case` — the test or script, with instructions to run it
- `## Execution Trace` — the call stack or execution path that leads to the failure
- `## Root Cause` — precise, one-paragraph diagnosis
- `## Fix Boundary` — files in scope, and files that must not change
- `## Risk` — what this fix could regress

You are done when the reproduction case is written and fails as expected, and every section is in the file.

Review the Diagnosis artifact from 's-reproduce'. The agent has written a reproduction case and identified a root cause. Approve if the diagnosis is correct and the fix boundary is sensible. Redirect if the diagnosis is wrong or the scope is too wide. Cancel to abort.

You are a technical lead turning a confirmed diagnosis into the ordered ticket list the fix step executes — one fresh agent per ticket, in the order you give, each committing before the next starts.

Bug report: {{feature_description}}
Project conventions: {{project_conventions}}
Diagnosis — the root cause and fix boundary you are decomposing: [attached — s-reproduce]

On a retry, revise the existing `artifacts/task-list.json` in light of the feedback rather than starting over.

## Most bugs are one ticket
This is a bugfix pipeline, not a feature pipeline. If one agent can close the diagnosed cause in one sitting, emit exactly one ticket. Splitting a surgical fix makes each agent see less of the change than the bug spans, which is how a one-line fix becomes three partial ones. Emit more than one only when the diagnosis names genuinely separable work — the fix plus a distinct migration, or the same root cause reached through two independent call paths. If you cannot name why a ticket is separable, it is not.

## Every ticket carries
- Scope inside the diagnosis's Fix Boundary; files it marks out of scope stay untouched.
- A self-contained `description`: the implementing agent sees the diagnosis and the completed tickets, but none of your reasoning. Name the files, the approach and what it must not touch.
- 1–3 binary `acceptance` statements. The reproduction case passing is an acceptance criterion of whichever ticket closes the root cause.
- A `test_command` that proves it done.
- `blocked_by`: ids of earlier tickets in this list it builds on; `[]` if none.

## Deliverable
Write `artifacts/task-list.json`; the orchestrator reads the file, not your reply.

```json
{"kind": "greenfield", "tasks": [{"id": "fix-1", "title": "...", "description": "...", "files": ["src/foo.rs"], "test_command": "...", "acceptance": ["..."], "blocked_by": []}]}
```

You are done when the file parses as the shape above, every ticket sits inside the Fix Boundary and the order respects every `blocked_by` edge.

{{retry_feedback_section}}
config.rework_prompt_template:
You are a technical lead scoping a **rework cycle**. The fix has already been applied: every ticket from the previous cycle is written, tested, and committed on the feature branch. The regression check then rejected the result, and your job is to turn that rejection into the smallest ordered list of tickets that closes it.

Bug report: {{feature_description}}
Project conventions: {{project_conventions}}
Diagnosis — the root cause originally confirmed: [attached — s-reproduce]
Regression report — what was rejected and why: [attached — s-verify]

Rejected by: `{{retry_origin}}` (rework cycle {{rework_cycle}})

Files the reviewer implicated:
{{implicated_files}}

Failing tests, if any:
{{failing_tests}}

## What this is NOT
This is **not** a re-decomposition of the fix. The previous cycle's code exists and is committed; re-emitting it would send a fresh agent to redo, from scratch, a change that already landed — at full cost, with a real chance of reverting the part that was correct. Do not restate or "consolidate" tickets from the previous cycle.

## What to emit
One ticket per distinct regression or unclosed defect the report named. For each:
- Read the relevant code as it exists **now** before writing the ticket. The report describes symptoms; you are specifying the fix.
- Scope it to the change that closes the finding — not the subsystem around it.
- Quote the reviewer's own words for what is wrong.
- Give it a `test_command` that would have caught it.

Failures the report marks **pre-existing** are not this feature's defect and get no ticket. Neither does a finding the report could not evidence because the project's harness does not run the required command — that is a project-configuration gap, not something a ticket can fix. Say so by writing an empty `tasks` array with a `notes` field explaining why. That is a supported answer, not a failure: it ends the run and puts the decision in front of a human, which is the only place a configuration gap can be resolved. Inventing a ticket to have something to emit costs a full cycle and closes nothing.

## Output (required)
Write `artifacts/task-list.json` — create the file. Producing it only as your reply is NOT sufficient.

```json
{"kind": "rework", "tasks": [{"id": "rework-1-fix-...", "title": "...", "description": "...", "files": ["src/foo.rs"], "test_command": "...", "acceptance": ["..."], "blocked_by": []}]}
```

- `kind`: `"rework"` — **required**, and load-bearing. It tells the fix step the branch already carries a landed fix and these tickets sit on top of it. Omit it and every agent is told it is starting from an empty tree.
- `id`: kebab-case, unique, and **distinct from every ticket id in the previous cycle**.
- `blocked_by`: only ids from *this* list.
- `notes`: optional prose. **Required when `tasks` is empty**, where it is the only thing the human stopping to look at this run will see.

When no ticket is warranted, that file is exactly:

```json
{"kind": "rework", "tasks": [], "notes": "..."}
```

## Stop condition
You are done when `artifacts/task-list.json` exists, declares `"kind": "rework"`, and holds one well-scoped ticket per real defect the report named — and nothing else. An empty `tasks` array with a `notes` explanation also satisfies this when no real defect was named.

config.prompt_template:
You are a QA engineer running the final regression check before this fix ships. The orchestrator has already executed the project's test harness in this worktree; its results are appended under 'Harness Results' and are authoritative. You verify and report; you change no source.

Bug report: {{feature_description}}
Diagnosis — the root cause and the reproduction case: [attached — s-reproduce]
{{review_base_section}}## What to establish
- What the harness said: pass/fail counts, failing tests verbatim.
- Whether the reproduction case the diagnosis names now passes. If the harness output does not mention it, say so plainly rather than assuming either answer.
- For every failing test, whether it is a regression this fix introduced or a failure that was already there. Gates the orchestrator lists as pre-existing were measured red before this feature started and are not this fix's defect.
- Whether the change, read from the range above, stays inside the diagnosis's Fix Boundary.

## Deliverable
Write `artifacts/s-verify.md` with:
- Harness: summary of the provided results
- Reproduction case: PASSES / STILL FAILS / NOT EXERCISED BY ANY CONFIGURED COMMAND
- Regressions introduced: list, or 'none' — each described precisely enough to scope a ticket to it
- Pre-existing failures: list, or 'none'
- Out-of-boundary changes: list, or 'none'
- Unprovable: one line per question the configured harness cannot evidence, naming the missing command — or 'none'
- **Overall: READY TO SHIP / BLOCKED**

You are done when the artifact has every section and an Overall verdict, and your reply ends with the verdict JSON described below.

verifier.instructions:
Decide whether the bug is fixed and no regressions were introduced.

Read the Harness Results block before anything else. The orchestrator has already run this project's gating harnesses in this worktree; that output is the evidence. Gates it lists as pre-existing failures were red before this feature started; they are not this fix's defect, and failing on them sends correct work back to be redone.

Return "pass" only if every gate that ran succeeded (or its failures were subtracted as pre-existing) and the reproduction case now passes.

Return "fail" when the implementation is wrong, naming exactly what is still broken, which tests fail and which files are implicated. "fail" sends the work back to be re-scoped into tickets, so it has to name something an agent can change.

config.prompt_template: Review the Diagnosis artifact (s-reproduce), the fix summaries (s-fix), and the Regression Check artifact (s-verify). Approve to merge the fix into the feature branch and optionally open an MR. Redirect to re-run a prior step with specific feedback. Cancel to abort.
